tasks.title: Fix apply_discount inverse formula in pricing.py
tasks.description: In pricing.py, change apply_discount so the discounted price is price * (1 - discount) instead of price * (1 + discount). Keep the existing validation that discount must be in [0, 1). This makes apply_discount(100, 0.2) == 80.0 and final_price(100, 0.2, 0.1) == 88.0.

tasks.title: Make report.py summarize use final_price instead of hardcoded 10%
tasks.description: In report.py, replace prices = [i["price"] * 0.9 for i in items] with prices = [final_price(i["price"], discount, tax_rate) for i in items], so summarize respects discount and tax_rate and matches order.py's order_total. Preserve the empty-items behavior (count 0, total 0.0, average 0.0, max_price 0.0).

tasks.title: Run shop test suite to verify report totals match order totals
tasks.description: Run pytest tests/test_shop.py and confirm all tests pass, especially test_discount, test_final_price, test_order_total, and test_summarize. Verify summarize(items, discount=0.2, tax_rate=0.1) returns total 132.0, average 66.0, max_price 88.0 and matches order_total(items, discount=0.2, tax_rate=0.1).

payload.summary: Fix the cross-file pricing inconsistency by correcting pricing.apply_discount to use (1 - discount) and updating report.summarize to call final_price with the provided discount and tax_rate instead of hardcoding a 10% multiplier. Then run the test suite to confirm report totals match order totals.

findings: pricing.py apply_discount currently returns price * (1 + discount), which incorrectly raises the price for a positive discount. It should be price * (1 - discount), keeping the existing ValueError guard for discount < 0 or discount >= 1.
pricing.py final_price correctly composes apply_discount then applies (1 + tax_rate), so fixing apply_discount makes final_price(100, 0.2, 0.1) == 88.0.
order.py order_total already uses final_price(item['price'], discount, tax_rate) and subtracts coupon; once apply_discount is fixed, order totals are correct.

report.py summarize imports final_price but does not use it; it hardcodes prices = [i['price'] * 0.9 for i in items], which ignores both discount and tax_rate and causes report totals to disagree with order totals.

report.py summarize should compute prices = [final_price(i['price'], discount, tax_rate) for i in items]; its empty-items behavior is already preserved by the conditional expressions for average and max_price.

tests/test_shop.py expectations confirm the intended behavior: apply_discount(100, 0.2) == 80.0, final_price(100, 0.2, 0.1) == 88.0, order_total([100,50], 0.2, 0.1) == 132.0, and summarize([100,50], 0.2, 0.1) total 132.0 / average 66.0 / max_price 88.0.

changes: pricing.py: apply_discount now returns price * (1 - discount) instead of price * (1 + discount), keeping the [0, 1) validation.
report.py: summarize now computes prices via final_price(i['price'], discount, tax_rate) instead of a hardcoded 10% multiplier (i['price'] * 0.9), preserving empty-items behavior.

payload.summary: Ran python3 -m pytest tests/test_shop.py -q: 7 passed in 0.01s. All tests (test_discount, test_discount_bounds, test_final_price, test_order_total, test_order_coupon, test_summarize, test_summarize_empty) pass. Lint/compile check (py_compile pricing.py report.py order.py) succeeded with no errors. The fixes to pricing.apply_discount (1 - discount) and report.summarize (final_price) are verified; report totals now match order totals.

suggestions: In report.py summarize, compute sum(prices) once and reuse it for total/average to avoid a duplicate sum over the list.
